name: Genetic Mixed Dermis Disorder

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Genetic Mixed Dermis Disorder Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of mixed dermal tissue types confirmed by histopathology
Identification of pathogenic mutation affecting dermal development genes
Clinically observable patchy or mosaic skin texture and pigmentation abnormalities
Exclusion of other known dermal disorders by clinical and laboratory evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met for diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing and skin biopsy are essential for confirmation

pathognomonic.symptomName: Patchy dermal mosaicism with mixed collagen and elastin abnormalities
searchTerms: patchy skin with mixed tissue defects
skin mosaic with collagen and elastin issues
irregular skin patches with connective tissue abnormalities

pathognomonic.symptomName: Segmental hypopigmentation and hyperpigmentation with irregular borders
searchTerms: skin patches with light and dark spots
areas of skin with mixed coloring

common.symptomName: Cutaneous atrophy with localized skin thinning

searchTerms: small visible blood vessels in skin

common.symptomName: Variable skin texture abnormalities including roughness and laxity
searchTerms: skin that feels uneven or lax

common.symptomName: Mild pruritus localized to affected skin areas

occasional.symptomName: Subcutaneous nodules within mixed dermal patches

searchTerms: excess hair growth on skin patches
increased hair in affected skin regions

occasional.symptomName: Mild joint hypermobility adjacent to affected skin areas
searchTerms: increased joint flexibility near affected skin

occasional.symptomName: Intermittent skin blistering in severely affected patches
searchTerms: skin blisters that come and go

rare.symptomName: Secondary bacterial skin infections in affected dermal regions
Associated mild scoliosis due to connective tissue abnormalities
searchTerms: minor spinal curvature due to tissue weakness

rare.symptomName: Localized sensory neuropathy over affected skin

laboratory: Histopathology showing mixed collagen and elastin fiber abnormalities
Genetic testing revealing mutations in dermal development genes
imaging: MRI may show localized soft tissue changes in severe cases
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes regulating dermal matrix composition and development
other: Clinical photographic documentation of skin mosaicism

distinguishingFeatures: Progressive skin hardening rather than mixed dermal tissue types
Predominantly pigmentary changes without mixed dermal histology

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin atrophy and ulceration
Development of secondary infections in affected skin
Signs of systemic involvement such as joint contractures or neuropathy
